score_scale: Each criterion scored 1-10. Overall = weighted mean. pass_threshold applies to the geometric-median aggregate across the panel.

criteria.name: The chorus works as a chant
criteria.anchor: The chorus is what a crowd sings at a rally without your recording: short (one to three lines, ~5 words per phrase), strong open vowels (ah/oh carry in a street), clear stress on strong beats, repeatable after one listen ('Get Up Stand Up' is the canon; Lyric Assistant protest-song guide; Berklee: 'the audience IS the chorus').
criteria.evidence: The lyric sheet (line lengths, repetition, vowel ends) and the style prompt.
criteria.guide: 10 = chorus is short, stress-matched, obviously shoutable, repeated verbatim. 7 = chantable with one weak line. 4 = chorus is poetic/abstract, not chantable. 1 = no distinct chorus.

criteria.name: Names the problem, not vague fury
criteria.anchor: Clarity: say who or what the problem is; abstract fury is less useful than a named target; concrete images turn slogans into stories ('One heater for three apartments', 'The bus stops running at midnight' — 5 specific grievances is the working exercise; Lyric Assistant). Verses carry the details; the chorus carries the demand in <= 5 words (Berklee: verses = your platform).
criteria.evidence: The lyric sheet: count concrete named targets/images vs abstract emotion words.
criteria.guide: 10 = verses name specific targets and images; the chorus states the demand plainly. 7 = one verse concrete, chorus clear. 4 = all-abstract emotion, nothing named. 1 = no discernible message.

criteria.name: Vocal reads as sincere, in a true voice
criteria.anchor: Protest vocals must reflect sincerity and honesty other songs don't require — 'the listener experiences a truth' (Berklee vocal-production note). Over-produced autotune kills the document function of the genre. The idiom's dynamic signature is wide-open: crest factor >= 10 dB is consistent with an unprocessed lead vocal.
criteria.evidence: The style prompt's vocal direction; crest_factor_db (an over-processed squash reads wrong for the idiom); unverifiable from measurements alone — say so.
criteria.guide: 10 = plain human vocal delivery claimed and dynamics consistent. 7 = claimed, unverified. 4 = heavily processed vocal claim. 1 = explicitly synthetic/robotic vocal on a protest document.

criteria.name: Words sit on the music naturally
criteria.anchor: Prosody: stressed syllables of key words on strong beats; speak the line from a rooftop — if the stress fights the meter, rewrite (Lyric Assistant). Test: a chorus line must scan in <= 5 strong beats and survive shouted repetition; scansion errors compound every repeated chorus pass.
criteria.evidence: The lyric sheet + ABC/transcript timing when present; bpm measurement for the meter.
criteria.guide: 10 = scansion fits the claimed meter with no forced stress. 7 = one forced line. 4 = several stresses land wrong. 1 = words fight the groove throughout.

criteria.name: Structure serves the movement
criteria.anchor: Working structures: verse-chorus-verse-chorus-bridge-chorus; intro-hook-verse-chorus-...-outro-chant; call-and-response (response <= 5 words) (Lyric Assistant structure options). Title = the main chorus line, not poetry (Berklee title rule).
criteria.guide: 10 = clear section map, chorus arrives early, title = chorus line. 7 = clear map, title drifts. 4 = structure present but muddy. 1 = no structure.

criteria.name: Master hits the lane loudness target
criteria.anchor: Streaming -14 LUFS (pipeline gate_loudness spec). Ad-suitability risk: audience-funded > ad-funded for this family (genres.yaml note) — loudness follows streaming target regardless.
criteria.guide: 10 = within +/-1 dB. 7 = within +/-3 dB. 4 = 3-6 dB off. 1 = 6+ dB off.

reject_signals: no chantable chorus (the genre's function fails)
vague fury with no named target or concrete image
heavy autotune/robotic processing claim on a protest document
lyrics that are a list of slogans with no verse-level story
